scope.summary: Run install_mcp_publisher as a subshell function that installs a guarded, quoted EXIT trap, so each invocation removes only its own mcp-publisher.XXXXXX work directory on success or failure; add three offline cleanup cases plus a caller-EXIT-trap-intact case to the supply-chain check.
out_of_scope: Changing the pinned mcp-publisher version, checksum source, or download URL
Deleting any temp directory other than the invocation's own mcp-publisher.XXXXXX work dir (R22)
The live MCP registry publish step (only the real release run R.7 exercises it)
GitHub-hosted runner behaviour; cleanup is proven offline with a stubbed curl and a synthetic archive

entry_points.name: Tier-A workflow supply-chain check (scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh)
entry_points.trace: bash scripts/workflow_supply_chain_check.sh exits 0; the three cases mcp_publisher_workdir_removed_on_success/_sha_mismatch/_download_failure each print {"expected":"absent","actual":"absent"} and mcp_publisher_caller_exit_trap_intact prints actual=fired; the pre-existing verify_sha256-before-tar ordering assertions also stay green

entry_points.name: install_mcp_publisher (invoked as `bash scripts/install_mcp_publisher.sh` from release.yml and publish-mcp.yml; sourced by the supply-chain check)
entry_points.trace: The same check sources the installer and drives install_mcp_publisher against a stubbed curl; on success the destination is installed and the work dir is gone, and on SHA mismatch / curl exit 22 the installer fails and the work dir is gone

limitations: Offline only: curl is stubbed through PATH and the platform metadata is overridden with a synthetic tar.gz fixture, so the real pinned publisher archive and the network path are not exercised (forbidden substitute per the bead).

The success case overrides mcp_publisher_platform to supply a matching digest for the synthetic fixture; the real pinned digests are only format-checked by the existing mapping assertions, not downloaded.
Proves the MCP registry publish step is not exercised, so registry publication is unproven.
Cleanup is demonstrated on this host's bash; GitHub-hosted self-hosted-runner reuse is only argued, not run.
